title: Atomic Theory and Structure - Chemistry - Modern
subject: Chemistry

questions.q: In the quantum mechanical model, an orbital is best defined as:
options: A circular path the electron follows.
A region of space where there is a high probability of finding an electron.
A fixed point where the electron is located.
A shell that contains exactly 8 electrons.
questions.explain: Unlike Bohr's orbits, quantum orbitals are 3D probability maps indicating where an electron is likely (usually 90% probability) to be found.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: The Heisenberg Uncertainty Principle states that it is impossible to simultaneously determine which two properties of a particle with perfect precision?
questions.explain: Werner Heisenberg showed that one cannot measure both the position and the momentum (velocity) of a quantum particle simultaneously with absolute precision.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What is the shape of an $(s)$ orbital?
questions.explain: $(s)$ orbitals are spherical in shape. $(p)$ orbitals are dumbbell-shaped.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: How does the quantum mechanical model of the atom differ from the Bohr model?
options: It treats the electron as a particle only.
It places electrons in fixed circular orbits.
It treats the electron mathematically as a wave and uses probability.
It assumes the nucleus is neutral.
questions.explain: The quantum mechanical model treats electrons as having wave-like properties and uses wave functions to calculate the probability of finding electrons (orbitals), rather than fixed paths (orbits).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What is the maximum number of electrons that can occupy a single orbital?
questions.explain: According to the Pauli Exclusion Principle, a single orbital can hold a maximum of 2 electrons, which must have opposite spins.
questions.subject: Chemistry
